Edema, Fluid Retention

Ailment edema fluid-retention circulatory lymphedema kidney heart

Evidence: peer_reviewed

Summary

Excess fluid accumulation in tissues causing swelling, typically in legs, ankles, or abdomen. Can be caused by heart conditions, kidney dysfunction, liver disease, or medication side effects.

Symptoms

  • swelling of extremities
  • pitting edema
  • weight fluctuation
  • shiny skin
  • reduced urine output

Treatment Approaches

  • Historical Traditional diuretic herbs (dandelion, celery seed, parsley) used for centuries to reduce swelling and support kidney function.
  • Proven Loop diuretics, ACE inhibitors, and aldosterone antagonists are evidence-based conventional treatments for edema secondary to heart, liver, or kidney disease.
  • Experimental CDS Protocol A (chlorine dioxide) explored anecdotally; no clinical evidence supports its use for edema reduction.
  • Conventional Compression stockings, low-sodium diet, and medical management of underlying cardiac, renal, or hepatic conditions.
